reasons: Status is well supported: the supplied paragraphs show dangling cross-references to a non-existent Section 20 (9.3 cites 'the remedies required by Section 20.5', 21.3 refers to 'its indemnification obligations', 19.5 to 'indemnity'), yet no indemnification clause exists — squarely the rule's walk-away case (no Vendor IP indemnity at all), so a 'missing' finding with an inserted clause is the correct treatment.

Redline reaches the preferred position with appropriate scope: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; customary exclusions (Customer modification, combination, Customer specifications); standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics with sensible settlement consent; and Customer's indemnity expressly narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, matching the model language.

Placement is per redline guidance — inserted after the warranty section (19.5) and before Section 21 Limitation of Liability — and the fifth inserted paragraph supplies the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies so it lands as the Section 20.5 already cross-referenced in Section 9.3.

Omission of the 3× super-cap is acceptable: that is a fallback mechanic, and the rationale correctly notes Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the liability cap.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, and explains both what was added and why; all deterministic checks pass. Minor drafting cleanup only: the inserted paragraphs reference 'Section 20.1(a)' while the rendered text shows no sub-numbering, and 'Affiliates'/'Vendor Technology' should be confirmed as defined terms in the Agreement.
